question:
Initially, a spinner points west. Chenille moves it clockwise \( 2 \frac{1}{4}\) revolutions and then counterclockwise \( 3 \frac{3}{4}\) revolutions. In what direction does the spinner point after the two moves?

[Figure 1](figures/2006_AMC_8_Q04_question_fig1.svg)
solution: A complete revolution returns the spinner to the same direction, so we can ignore the complete revolutions in both moves. The first move therefore has the same effect as \(\frac14\) revolution clockwise, taking the spinner from west to north. The second move has the same effect as \(\frac34\) revolution counterclockwise. These three quarter-turns take it from north to west, then south, then east. Thus the spinner points east, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
